Constructing chiral aza-quaternary carbon centers
by enantioselective carbonylative Heck reaction of
o-iodoanilines with allenes †
Zhengshuai Xu, Chaoren Shen,
 Hongru Zhang, Peng Wang and Kaiwu Dong
 *
The construction of chiral aza-quaternary carbon centers via C–N bond formation has been achieved by
a palladium-catalyzed asymmetric carbonylative Heck reaction of o-iodoanilines with allenes, providing
chiral dihydroquinolinone derivatives with moderate to high yield and enantiomeric ratio (er). The er could
be improved to 99/1 through the recrystallization of the isolated products. Adding o-iodoaniline into the
reaction by syringe pump was crucial to diminish the side reactions of reactive o-iodoanilines and
improve the chemoselectivity. Utilizing the chirality induction of an assembled aza-quaternary stereogenic
center, molecules bearing vicinal chiral quaternary carbon centers or multiple chiral centers can be
rapidly prepared.
The intrinsic properties of a chiral quaternary carbon center
in terms of biological characteristics, i.e., activity, metab-
olism, solubility, and hydrophobicity, endow the e ﬃcient
catalytic methods for its construction with long-lasting
research importance.
1 In particular, the crucial influence of
the absolute configuration of the chiral aza-quaternary
carbon center, which constitutes one of the ubiquitous struc-
tural units in natural products and pharmaceuticals
(Scheme 1A), 2 on biological activity 3 gives significance to the
building of such a stereocenter. In this context, diverse
methods via C–C bond formation for preparing optically
active molecules bearing an aza-quaternary carbon center
have been well exploited. For example, the catalytic asym-
metric addition of carbonic nucleophiles onto ketimines
2b,4
and the enantioselective substitution of carbonic electro-
philes with α-nitrogen substituted pro-chiral carbonic nucleo-
philes5 are commonly used protocols. In sharp contrast, cata-
lytic asymmetric approaches via C–N bond formation have
been far less explored, although they could provide direct and
convenient access to these chiral amines. As we know, stereo-
selective protocols include aza-Michael addition, 6 aerobic oxi-
dation of β-ketocarbonyls, 7 intramolecular radical bicycliza-
tion,8 and cycloaddition 9 (Scheme 1B).
To meet the demand for accessing structurally complex
chiral amines from comparatively common and inexpensive
starting materials, diversifying the catalytic approaches to a

chiral aza-quaternary carbon center via C–N bond formation is
imperative.10 Meanwhile, among the above-mentioned methods
of access, there is still a lack of e ﬀective methods with the capa-
bility of synchronously forming multiple bonds. As a powerful
strategy to achieve the simultaneous formation of C –Na n dC –C
bonds across alkenes, asymmetric carboamination is a potent
but almost unexplored C –N bond formation route to e ﬃciently
assemble a chiral aza-quaternary carbon center,
11 and its poten-
tial has yet to be exploited.12
Similar to the merits of carboamination, the palladium-cat-
alysed carbonylative Heck reaction 13 also possesses the capa-
bility of simultaneously constructing two carbon –carbon
bonds, and has been recognized as an important tool in the
construction of α,β-unsaturated carbonyl compounds 14 and
heterocycles.15 Considering the common features of carboami-
nation and the palladium-catalysed carbonylative Heck reac-
tion and inspired by the work of Alper et al. on palladium-cata-
lysed multicomponent achiral cyclocarbonylation under high
CO pressure at 90 –100 °C (Scheme 1C),
12 we intended to
utilize a combination of these two powerful approaches to
diversify the access to a chiral aza-quaternary stereogenic
center via C–N bond formation and elevate the synthetic
eﬃciency with a more active chiral palladium catalyst under
milder conditions that are beneficial to inhibiting background
reactions and acquiring high enantioselectivity while still
retaining good carbonylative selectivity ( e.g. lower CO pressure/
reaction temperature and shorter reaction time). Herein, we
report a palladium-catalysed enantioselective carbonylative
Heck reaction between o-iodoanilines and allenes involving an
alkene carboamination step (Scheme 1D). A variety of dihydro-
quinolinone derivatives containing a chiral aza-quaternary
carbon center and one convertible alkene functional group
was a ﬀorded with moderate to high yield and enantiomeric
ratio (e.r.). Based on this reaction, a set of e ﬃcient methods
for the rapid construction of multiple chiral centers with good
yield and diastereoselectivity was developed.
To explore the feasibility of synchronously assembling an
aza-quaternary carbon stereocenter and accomplishing the for-
mation of multiple C –C and C –N bonds, 2-iodoaniline 1a and
allene 2a were selected as model substrates for a palladium-
catalysed enantioselective carbonylative Heck reaction.
Initially, a series of monodentate and bidentate privileged
chiral ligands (29 chiral ligands) with di ﬀerent coordinating
atoms was tested by employing tris(dibenzylideneacetone)
dipalladium(0) as a palladium source and N,N-diisopropyl-
ethylamine as an acid scavenger in N,N-dimethylacetamide
solution under CO atmosphere at 80 °C for 24 h (for detailed
results see Table S1 in ESI †). Among these ligands, only axially
bidentate phosphines, such as BINAP and substituent-modi-
fied MeO-BIPHEP ligands, could obtain the desired annulation
product 3a in either moderate yield or medium enantio-
selectivity. The demands for good product yield and high
enantioselectivity failed to be met at the same time.
Considering the relatively high yield obtained by ( R)-BINAP
(88%) and the relatively good enantioselectivity using ( R)-
BTFM-GarPhos (86 : 14 e.r.), we employed these two ligands to
further explore the optimal conditions by solvent screening,
tuning the Pd/P molar ratio, and CO pressure (Tables S2 –S5 in
ESI†). However, neither the yield nor the er was significantly
improved. The palladium-to-phosphorus ratio has a sophisti-
cated but noticeable impact on the yield of 3a, i.e., a lower Pd/
P ratio (10 mol% Pd loading) diminished the yield of 3a (for a
detailed comparison see Table S5 in ESI †). During the course
of optimization, the prevailing imbalances between the yield
of 3a and the conversion of substrate 1a as well as the unequal
conversion of substrates 1a and
2a were observed. Specifically,
in almost all circumstances when adding one equivalent of 1a
and two equivalents of 2a, 1a was quantitatively consumed
and more than one equivalent of 2a was detected after the
reaction, wherein product 3a was obtained in only low to mod-
erate yield. Compared with the reported Heck cyclization of
EWG-substituted cumulated dienes with similar iodo sub-
strates,
16 allene 1a is much less activated due to the absence of
EWG.17 No GC-detectable or TLC-observable side products
from the inter/intramolecular aminocarbonylation of 1a (e.g.
isatin18 or 2-amino-N-(2-iodophenyl)-benzamide19) were identi-
fied. When 2-iodoaniline was replaced by the less reactive
2-bromoaniline or 2-amino phenyltriflate, no conversion of
these substrates was observed (for detailed results see Table S7
in ESI †). Even in the absence of phosphine ligands, 2-iodoani-
line could be quantitatively consumed under a CO atmosphere
with Pd
2(dba)3, PdI 2 or Pd/C, but only a little racemic product
3a was generated (Table S6 in ESI †). These experimental
results suggest that 2-iodoaniline is apparently much more
reactive than allene 2a in the presence of a palladium catalyst,
which leads to the swift consumption of substrate 1a through
complicated side reactions.
Based on the above findings, we conjectured that keeping
the concentration of substrate low in the reaction might
prevent these side reactions resulting from the high reactivity
of 1a and thus attain better chemoselectivity. Moreover, trans-
forming the neutral palladium intermediates to the cationic
palladium species by silver salt additives clearly exhibited
benefits to the chemoselectivity and enantioselectivity for the
asymmetric Heck reaction.
20 Therefore, both altering the
manner of feeding the substrate into the reaction solution and
adding a silver salt were examined (Table 1). Compared to the
result of adding the substrate in a one-portion manner (entry
1), adding 1a into the reaction solution in a dropwise manner
by a syringe pump over 6 hours indeed elevated the yield of
product 3a and preserved the good enantioselectivity (entry 2).
Utilizing AgBF
4 as the additive and feeding 1a into the reaction
solution by programmed syringe pump over 6 hours could
reduce the demand of allene 2a and simultaneously obtained
a much higher yield of 3a than in the one-portion addition
manner (entry 3 versus entry 4). Accelerating the rate of
addition led to a decline in product yield (entry 5). Using
AgOTf instead of AgBF
4 and adding 1a by syringe pump could
also have the e ﬀect of drastically inhibiting the undesirable
side reaction (entry 6), but the yield and enantioselectivity are
slightly inferior to those obtained using AgBF
4. These results
clearly exhibited the usefulness of utilizing a syringe pump in

eliminating the side reactions encountered in the batch-type
carbonylative reaction. Gratifyingly, enantiomeric enrichment
was observed for the carbonylation product, and 3a was
aﬀorded as a solid with 99 : 1 e.r. and 66% yield after recrystal-
lization with petroleum ether/dichloromethane.
With the optimized reaction conditions in hand, we investi-
gated the substrate scope of o-iodoanilines and allenes
(Scheme 2). The carbonylative Heck reaction between o-iodoa-
nilines 1 and allenes 2 bearing di ﬀerent functional groups
gave chiral methylene-2,3-dihydro-1 H-quinolin-4-ones in mod-
erate to excellent yields with a good enantiomeric ratio. Both
electron-rich and electron-deficient substitutes on the phenyl
ring of o-iodoaniline substrate 1 or 3-phenyl 1,2-butadiene 2
are well tolerated ( 3b–3k, 3m–3q). The bromo and chloro
groups on the phenyl ring of the substrates remained intact by
this protocol and the corresponding carbonylative Heck reac-
tion products were a ﬀorded in moderate to good yields with a
good enantiomeric ratio ( 3c–3e, 3j, 3o). These halogen substi-
tuents provide potential reaction sites for the further trans-
formation of products via transition metal-catalysed cross
coupling. The thienyl substituent in the allene substrate ( 3l)
was also compatible with this protocol. Switching the phenyl
group on the allene substrate to a fused aryl ring ( 3r) had little
impact on yield or enantioselectivity. Attaching a methyl sub-
stituent onto the amino group of o-iodoaniline largely reduced
its reactivity, which led to the poor conversion and low yield of
3s. Modifying the amino group of o-iodoaniline with acetyl
resulted in intramolecular cyclocarbonylation forming
2-methyl-4H-3,1-benzoxazin-4-one,
21 while a series of insepar-
able side products was generated for N-tosyl o-iodoaniline.
Again, we found that the major enantiomer of carbonylative
annulation products could be further enriched to higher
optical purity by recrystallizing the isolated reaction products
(e.g. 3c and 3f ). The absolute configuration of 3a was deter-
mined to be ( S) by X-ray crystallographic analysis.
Considering the distinct e ﬀect of the substrate feeding
manner on the product yield and to further prove the
reliability of this protocol, the scale-up of this carbonylative
Heck reaction between substrates 1a and 2a was examined and
it showed that the good chemoselectivity and enantioselectivity
were unaﬀected at a larger reaction scale (1.0 mmol) with less
catalyst loading (Scheme 3). By recrystallizing the isolated
product in a mixed solvent of petroleum ether and dichloro-
methane, the chiral carbonylative product 3a with high optical

purity (99 : 1 e.r.) was obtained in 60% yield (Scheme 3). More
than building up the aza-quaternary stereogenic center, the
other noteworthy feature of this palladium-catalysed asym-
metric carbonylative Heck reaction is the generation of a di-
substituted terminal alkene functional group, which is not
only conjugated to the implanted carbonyl group, but is also
adjacent to the aza-quaternary carbon stereocenter. It provides
a valuable reaction site to produce vicinal or multiple chiral
centers by asymmetric induction relying on the intervention of
the aza-quaternary carbon stereocenter. To validate this design
of readily constructing vicinal or multiple chiral centers within
two steps, we selected the asymmetric three-component 1,3-
dipolar cycloaddition of readily accessible ethyl 2-diazoacetate,
nitrosobenzene with alkene 3a,
22 as well as the asymmetric
Michael addition of para-methylthiol or indole nucleophile on
Michael acceptor 3a23 (Scheme 3). To our delight, through the
cycloaddition of an in situ formed active nitrone intermediate
onto the alkene group of 3a, spiromethylene-2,3-dihydro-1 H-
quinolin-4-one isoxazolidine 4a, which possesses three chiral
stereogenic centers including a pair of vicinal aza-quaternary
and oxa-quaternary stereocenters, could be obtained in high
yield with good enantioselectivity and diastereoselectivity
under mild conditions. By Michael addition onto the carbonyl
conjugated C –C double bond of 3a, chiral thioether 5a and
chiral indole derivative 6a, both bearing a pair of vicinal chiral
centers, were a ﬀorded in good yield with excellent enantio-
meric ratio and good diastereoselectivity (Scheme 3).
Owing to the di ﬃculty that 1,3-dipolar cycloaddition
product 4a was rather liable to form a non-crystalline solid
even by various crystallization techniques, the e ﬀort to deter-
mine the configuration of three chiral centers in 4a by X-ray
diﬀraction failed. Thus, we employed density functional theory
(DFT) calculations to predict the configuration and elucidate
the high diastereoselectivity of this 1,3-dipolar cycloaddition.
Since the in situ formed active nitrone intermediate 1-ethylcar-
boxy N-phenylmethanimine oxide has four di ﬀerent isomers
consisting of ( E)- or ( Z)-configurations on the C –N double
bond and s- cis or s-trans conformations
24 and pondering these
two factors: (i) the equilibrium between these isomers is
dependent on the polarity of solvent 25 and the presence of
Lewis acids; 26 (ii) product 4a has eight potential enantiomers
and diastereomers, we searched out a total of sixteen 1,3-
dipolar cycloaddition transition states for the addition of
nitrone intermediate 1-ethylcarboxy N-phenylmethanimine
oxide onto the alkene group neighbouring the ( S)-configur-
ation quaternary center in 3a (for more details see ESI †). By
comparing the potential energy location of these transition
states in the solvation of dichloroethane, we found that two
transition states, both of which are towards generating an ( S)-
configuration oxa-quaternary carbon center and ( R)-configur-
ation aza-tertiary carbon center (Fig. 1), are much more energe-
tically advantageous than the other fourteen transition states
(for detailed results and analysis see ESI †). This outcome is
highly consistent with the observed high enantioselectivity
and diastereoselectivity of cycloaddition product 4a and
revealed the good chiral induction contributed from the
carbonylation-implanted aza-quaternary stereocenter. The suc-
cessful implementation of these conversions proves the potent
utilization of an aza-quaternary stereocenter assembled
through this palladium-catalysed asymmetric carbonylative
Heck reaction in the rapid construction of multiple chiral
centers.
In summary, an e ﬃcient method for the construction of a
chiral aza-quaternary carbon center via C–N bond formation
by a palladium-catalysed asymmetric carbonylative Heck reac-
tion of o-iodoanilines with allenes was developed. Adopting
the dropwise addition manner in this batch-type reaction
could e ﬀectively inhibit the proceeding of side reactions due
to the high reactivity of the o-iodoaniline substrate. By utilizing
the aza-quaternary stereogenic center to impose chirality
induction in the subsequent alkene transformation, highly
functionalized and otherwise inaccessible molecules contain-
ing a pair of vicinal chiral centers can be facilely prepared.
Conﬂicts of interest
There are no conflicts to declare.
